quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind. For larger animals, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: Hand signals can be used instead of or with turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT good safety advice?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Don't drag your feet—they could catch and cause you to lose control. Always look for other traffic.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Not allow for eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your vision to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield is scratch-free, resists damage, gives a clear side view, fastens securely, allows air to flow to prevent fogging, and fits over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Try to hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle just before you hit it.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks up on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle's wind blast hits you, where should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to react if a wind blast disturbs your control.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.
questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: If the throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle gets stuck, try twisting it back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is good for staying close while giving each rider space. Use a single-file formation when going around curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding, you should not:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Reach the handle grips with your arms slightly bent.
Keep your feet on the footrests.
Hold your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent so you can easily control the motorcycle. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your feet on the footrests and your knees against the gas tank to help keep your balance during turns.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press lightly on the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: If you must swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press lightly on the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should not:

options.text: Ride too close behind other riders.
Place inexperienced riders just behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change riding formations too often.
questions.explanation: Groups should take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Inexperienced riders should ride behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Use a staggered formation to keep enough space between riders.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, the rider should:

options.text: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean opposite to the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while leaning their body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean at the same angle as your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.
